kind.pick: What kind of toy or game franchise is {label}?
kind.match: Match each franchise to its kind.
kind.odd: Three of these are {value} franchises. Which one isn't?

rows.label: Dungeons & Dragons
rows.hook: sent players on epic quests where a dice roll decides whether their hero succeeds or fails

rows.label: Transformers
rows.hook: stars robots that disguise themselves as cars, trucks, and other machines

rows.label: My Little Pony
rows.hook: follows a group of small, colorful horses whose adventures center on friendship and magic

rows.label: Masters of the Universe
rows.hook: follows the musclebound hero He-Man as he defends his planet with a magic sword

rows.label: Rummikub
rows.description: tile-based game for two to four players
rows.hook: challenges players to arrange numbered pieces into runs and sets before their opponents do

rows.label: Beyblade
rows.description: a line of spinning-top toys originally developed by a Japanese toy company
rows.hook: battles when players launch a whirling toy into an arena hoping to be the last one standing

rows.label: G.I. Joe
rows.description: American line of action figures and media franchise
rows.hook: follows a team of elite soldiers who battle the terrorist organization Cobra

rows.label: Care Bears
rows.hook: gives each of its fuzzy, pastel-colored figures a special symbol on its tummy representing a feeling

rows.label: Monster High
rows.hook: follows fashionable teenage children of famous movie monsters at their spooky school

rows.label: Hot Wheels
rows.hook: makes miniature vehicles built for speed, often raced down orange plastic tracks

rows.label: Sea-Monkeys
rows.hook: hatches from a powder added to water and grows into tiny swimming creatures kept in a tank

rows.label: bingo
rows.hook: calls out numbers that players mark on cards, racing to complete a row before anyone else

rows.label: Matchbox
rows.hook: makes pocket-sized toy cars once famous for fitting in a shirt pocket, now collected by adults
